title: Bauxite Washing Drum
model_title: Bauxite Washing (Scrubbing) Drum with Trommel Discharge Screen

introduction.definition: A bauxite washing (scrubbing) drum tumbles crushed bauxite with water. Lifters raise the lumps and drop them so they rub against each other and clay is washed off. A trommel screen at the discharge separates washed bauxite from the clay-rich fines, which carry much of the reactive silica.
applications: Beneficiation of lateritic/karstic bauxites with clay
key_points: Trommel splits washed product and fines

pressure.title: Attrition scrubbing removes clay and reactive silica
pressure.description: Lifters raise the bauxite and drop it, so lumps rub and impact each other in water. Fine clay (often rich in reactive silica, which costs caustic soda in digestion) is washed off and leaves with the trommel undersize. Drum speed is typically ~ 50–75 % of critical speed.

video_tutorials.title: Bauxite Washing Drum — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Bauxite Washing Drum.
A bauxite washing (scrubbing) drum tumbles crushed bauxite with water.
Lifters raise the lumps and drop them so they rub against each other and clay is washed off.
A trommel screen at the discharge separates washed bauxite from the clay-rich fines, which carry much of the reactive silica.
Typical applications include beneficiation of lateritic/karstic bauxites with clay; removing reactive silica before digestion.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Scrubbing Drum: Shell with Liners / Lifters (rotates), Scrubbing Drum: Riding Tyres & Girth Gear (turn with the shell).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Bauxite Washing Drum works.
Bauxite and water enter through the feed chute.
The drum turns; lifters raise and drop the lumps.

Products leave via chutes.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Bauxite Washing Drum.
Check liners, sprays and trommel.
Gear mesh and roller alignment.
Reline drum.
Watch for liner wear: holes, noise. Common cause: abrasion.
Watch for screen blinding: fines in product. Common cause: sticky clay.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
